recipes.name: Balanced cone
recipes.tuningNote:
Tastes sour or thin? Grind finer.
Tastes bitter or dry? Grind coarser.

steps.instruction: Wet every ground and give the dripper a gentle swirl.
Pour in slow circles from the centre outward.
Pour to the final weight, keeping the bed level.
Let the bed drain completely.

recipes.name: Even flat bed
recipes.tuningNote: If the cup is muddy, pour more gently and swirl less.

steps.instruction: Cover the bed evenly and wait for it to settle.
Pour steadily in a wide spiral.
Finish the pour in one smooth pass.
Swirl once to flatten the bed.
Let the bed drain completely.

recipes.name: Steep then release
recipes.tuningNote:
Tastes bitter or heavy? Steep for less time.
Tastes sour or sharp? Steep for longer.

steps.instruction: Close the valve before adding anything.
Pour all the water quickly and evenly.
Stir the slurry a few times.
Let it steep.
Set it on your mug or carafe, then open the valve.
Let the coffee drain completely.

recipes.name: Classic press
recipes.tuningNote: For a cleaner cup, skim the top and let it settle before pressing.

steps.instruction: Pour all the water over the grounds.
Stir gently to break the crust.
Place the lid on and steep.
Press the plunger down slowly and pour right away.

recipes.name: Short inverted press
recipes.tuningNote: Dripping through the plug means the plunger is not seated; reseat before pouring.

steps.instruction: Seat the plunger a little way into the chamber, upside down.
Add the grounds, then pour all the water.
Stir briefly.
Steep.
Fit the filter cap, then flip it onto your mug or carafe.
Press down steadily until it stops.

recipes.name: Espresso starting point
recipes.tuningNote:
Runs fast and tastes sour? Grind finer.
Runs slow and tastes bitter? Grind coarser.

steps.instruction: Start the shot and watch the yield on the scale.
Stop the shot at the target weight.

recipes.name: Flash-chilled pour over
recipes.tuningNote: Hot water is the brewed amount; the ice sits in the carafe and melts into the cup.

steps.instruction: Wet the bed. The ice is already in the carafe.
Pour in slow circles.
Pour to the final hot-water weight.
Swirl the carafe to finish chilling.

recipes.name: Cold steep concentrate
recipes.tuningNote: Dilute to taste when serving; steep longer in a cooler place.

steps.instruction: Add cool water over the grounds.
Stir until no dry pockets remain.
Cover and steep in the fridge, then strain.

recipes.name: Strong cup
recipes.tuningNote: Tetsu Kasuya's 4:6: the last 60% of the water in three pours makes a stronger cup.

steps.instruction: Pour 60 g in a spiral and let it drain.
Pour 60 g once the bed runs dry.
Pour 60 g.
Pour 60 g.
Pour the last 60 g.
Remove the dripper as it finishes.

recipes.name: Lighter, sweeter cup
recipes.tuningNote: Tetsu Kasuya's 4:6: the last 60% in one pour gives a lighter body that lets sweetness show.

steps.instruction: Pour 60 g in a spiral and let it drain.
Pour 60 g once the bed runs dry.
Pour the remaining 180 g in one go.
Remove the dripper at about 2:45.

recipes.name: Hoffmann's big V60
recipes.tuningNote: Two cups. Stir and swirl so the bed ends flat; if it chokes, grind coarser.

steps.instruction: Pour 60 g from the centre out.
Swirl until there are no dry lumps.
Pour to 300 g, centre out then in circles.
Pour to 500 g in the centre, keeping it full.
Stir gently one way, then the other.
Swirl two or three times.
Let it drain fully, about 3:30.

recipes.name: Many small pours
recipes.tuningNote: Pour about every 25 seconds, whenever the slurry drops below the grounds.

steps.instruction: Pour 50 g in circles from the centre out.
Pour to 100 g.
Pour to 150 g.
Pour to 200 g.
Pour to 250 g.
Pour to 300 g, one pass over the filter ridges.
Pour the last 55 g.
Let it drain; aim to finish by 3:15 to 3:45.

recipes.name: Three big pours
recipes.tuningNote: Fewer, bigger pours. Use just-off-boil water.

steps.instruction: Pour 90 g in a circle.
Pour to 250 g.
Pour to 350 g.
Let it drain, about 3:00 in all.

recipes.name: Classic 1:16
recipes.tuningNote: A steady four-pour recipe; finish between 3:00 and 3:30.

steps.instruction: Pour 50 g and wait 30 seconds.
Pour about 100 g in circles.
Pour about 100 g.
Pour the last 70 g.
Let it drain fully.

recipes.name: Sweet hybrid
recipes.tuningNote: Percolate hot, then steep cooler: cool the kettle to about 70 °C before closing the valve.

steps.instruction: Start with the valve open.
Pour 60 g from the centre out.
Spiral pour to 120 g, then add cold water to the kettle.
Close the valve.
Pour to 280 g at about 70 °C.
Open the valve to drain.
Close it again at 3:00 even if it is still dripping.

recipes.name: Water first, long steep
recipes.tuningNote: Water goes in before the coffee, so every ground is wet at once.

steps.instruction: Close the valve.
Pour all the water, then add the coffee.
Stir until saturated.
Steep.
Break the crust so the grounds sink.
Open the valve to drain.
Should finish about a minute later.

recipes.name: Bright light-roast steep
recipes.tuningNote: Made for light roasts: boiling water and a short steep.

steps.instruction: Close the valve.
Pour all the water, then add the coffee.
Stir until saturated, then cover.
Steep.
Stir the crust so the grounds settle.
Open the valve to drain.
Let it drain, about a minute.

recipes.name: Clean, no-sludge cup
recipes.tuningNote: The long settle makes the cup clean. Don't push the plunger down; pour slowly.

steps.instruction: Pour all 500 g in about 10 seconds.
Steep.
Break the crust with a spoon.
Skim off the foam with two spoons, then wait for the grounds to sink.
Set the plunger at the surface without pressing, and pour slowly.

recipes.name: Big batch
recipes.tuningNote: For a full 1-litre press.
recipes.credit: Honest Coffee Guide, basic French press

steps.instruction: Pour 180 g and wet every ground.
Stir.
Pour to 720 g.
Put the lid on and steep.
Press gently and slowly.

recipes.name: Strong cup
recipes.tuningNote: A tighter 1:14 ratio for more body. Too heavy: go back to the classic.

steps.instruction: Pour all the water over the grounds.
Stir gently.
Lid on and steep.
Press slowly and pour right away.

recipes.name: Bloom and steep
recipes.tuningNote: A short bloom first, then the rest of the water.

steps.instruction: Seat the plunger in the chamber, upside down.
Pour 30 g.
Stir 3 or 4 times.
Let it bloom.
Pour to 200 g.
Fit a rinsed filter cap, push out the air, and flip onto the cup.
Press gently for about 30 seconds.

recipes.name: Quick and bright
recipes.tuningNote: Fast and bright. Press ends early: grind finer. Runs long: coarser.
recipes.credit: Honest Coffee Guide, basic inverted AeroPress

steps.instruction: Seat the plunger in the chamber, upside down.
Pour 200 g in about 10 seconds.
Stir 3 or 4 times.
Steep.
Fit the cap, push out the air, and flip.
Press slowly, about 30 seconds.

recipes.name: Strong cup
recipes.tuningNote: A 1:12 ratio for a heavier cup; top up with hot water if it is too strong.

steps.instruction: Seat the plunger in the chamber, upside down.
Pour all the water.
Stir briefly.
Steep.
Fit the cap and flip onto the cup.
Press down steadily until it stops.

recipes.name: Sweet ristretto
recipes.tuningNote: 1:1.5. Shorter and syrupy; about 23 s for dark roasts, 30 s for lighter ones.

steps.instruction: Start the shot and watch the yield.
Stop at 30 g.

recipes.name: Big 21 g double
recipes.tuningNote: 1:2 from a bigger basket, a classic café double.

steps.instruction: Start the shot and watch the yield.
Stop at 42 g.

recipes.name: Bright lungo
recipes.tuningNote: About 1:2.8. Lighter body, more clarity; good for light roasts.

steps.instruction: Start the shot and watch the yield.
Stop at 50 g.

recipes.name: Iced V60 for two
recipes.tuningNote: Grind slightly finer than for hot filter. Stir into the ice when done.

steps.instruction: Pour 75 g. 200 g of ice is already in the carafe.
Stir the bed to wet it evenly.
Pour slowly to 300 g by about 3:00.
Stir the coffee into the ice.

recipes.name: 40% ice
recipes.tuningNote: Ice is 40% of the total water, so the cup lands at full strength.

steps.instruction: Pour 60 g. 200 g of ice is in the carafe.
Pour to 180 g.
Pour to 300 g.
Swirl the carafe until the ice is mostly melted.

recipes.name: Strong iced
recipes.tuningNote: Less hot water and more ice for a punchier, colder cup.

steps.instruction: Wet the bed. The ice is already in the carafe.
Pour in slow circles.
Pour to the final hot-water weight.
Swirl to finish chilling.

recipes.name: Room-temperature bottle
recipes.tuningNote: Ready to drink, no dilution needed. Coarse grind, like a French press.

steps.instruction: Add the water over the grounds.
Shake or stir gently.
Steep up to 18 hours at room temperature, shake again, then strain.

recipes.name: Strong concentrate
recipes.tuningNote: 1:5. Dilute about 1:1 with water or milk when serving.

steps.instruction: Add cool water over the grounds.
Stir until no dry pockets remain.
Cover and steep about 16 hours, then strain.

recipes.name: Light concentrate
recipes.tuningNote: 1:5.6. Softer; dilute less when serving.

steps.instruction: Add cool water over the grounds.
Stir until no dry pockets remain.
Cover and steep about 16 hours, then strain.

recipes.name: Classic stovetop
recipes.tuningNote:
Tastes sharp or thin? Grind a little finer.
Tastes bitter or burnt? Take it off the heat sooner.

steps.instruction: Fill the base with hot water just under the valve. Fill the basket level; don't tamp.
Screw it together and set it on medium heat with the lid open.
Coffee starts to rise. Turn the heat down.
When it turns pale and starts to gurgle, take it off the heat and cool the base under the tap.

recipes.name: Hot start
recipes.tuningNote: Starting with just-boiled water shortens the time on the heat, which keeps it from tasting burnt.

steps.instruction: Fill the base with just-boiled water to the valve. Use a towel; it's hot.
Assemble and set it on medium-low heat, lid open.
Coffee starts to rise. Keep the flow slow and steady.
At the first gurgle, take it off the heat and cool the base.

recipes.name: Low and slow
recipes.tuningNote: A gentle flame gives a rounder, less bitter cup. Take longer, not hotter.

steps.instruction: Fill the base with cold water to the valve and fill the basket level.
Assemble and set it on the lowest flame, lid open.
Coffee starts to rise. Leave the flame low.
When the flow turns pale, take it off the heat and cool the base.

recipes.name: Standard
recipes.tuningNote:
Tastes sour? Grind finer or steep longer.
Tastes bitter? Grind coarser or press sooner.

steps.instruction: Pour all the water over the grounds.
Stir three times.
Set the plunger on top to stop the drip.
Press down slowly and steadily for about 30 seconds.

recipes.name: Bypass
recipes.tuningNote: Brews a strong shot, then tops it up. Change the top-up to taste.

steps.instruction: Pour 100 g of water over the grounds.
Stir well so every ground is wet.
Set the plunger on top to stop the drip.
Press slowly into the mug.
Top up with 100 g of hot water.

recipes.name: One-minute
recipes.tuningNote: Hotter water and a finer grind make up for the short time.

steps.instruction: Pour all the water quickly.
Stir five times.
Set the plunger on top.
Press steadily to the end.

recipes.name: Classic
recipes.tuningNote:
Draining slowly? Grind coarser.
Tastes thin? Grind finer.

steps.instruction: Rinse the paper first, then wet the bed and let it bloom.
Pour in slow circles to 300 g.
Pour to the final weight.
Let it drain. Lift the filter out when the bed is dry.

recipes.name: Big batch for two
recipes.tuningNote: A bigger bed drains slower; a slightly coarser grind keeps the time in check.

steps.instruction: Wet the whole bed and let it bloom.
Pour in slow circles to 400 g.
Pour to the final weight.
Let it drain fully.

recipes.name: Iced Chemex
recipes.tuningNote: Hot water is the brewed amount; the ice sits in the carafe and melts into the cup.

steps.instruction: Ice is already in the carafe. Wet the bed and let it bloom.
Pour in slow circles to the final hot-water weight.
Let it drain, then swirl the carafe to finish chilling.

recipes.name: Standard pot
recipes.tuningNote:
Tastes weak? Use more coffee, not a finer grind.
Tastes bitter? Grind a little coarser.

steps.instruction: Fill the reservoir with fresh cold water and fill the basket.
Start the machine.
When it stops dripping, swirl the pot before you pour.

recipes.name: Single mug
recipes.tuningNote: A small batch brews fast; a slightly finer grind keeps it from tasting thin.

steps.instruction: Fill the reservoir with one mug of water and fill the basket.
Start the machine.
When it stops dripping, it's ready.

recipes.name: Strong
recipes.tuningNote: More coffee for the same water gives a bolder pot without a bitter grind.

steps.instruction: Fill the reservoir and fill the basket a little fuller than usual.
Start the machine.
Swirl the pot before you pour.

recipes.name: Three-cup pot
recipes.tuningNote: A small pot heats fast; keep the flame low so it doesn't scorch.

steps.instruction: Fill the base with hot water to the valve and fill the basket level.
Assemble and set it on low to medium heat, lid open.
Coffee starts to rise. Turn the heat down.
At the first gurgle, take it off the heat and cool the base.

recipes.name: Light and long
recipes.tuningNote: Less coffee, cooler water and a longer steep give a lighter, tea-like cup.

steps.instruction: Pour all the water over the grounds.
Stir gently twice.
Set the plunger on top to stop the drip.
Press slowly to the end.

recipes.name: Bright
recipes.tuningNote: More water for the coffee and hotter water bring out brighter, lighter notes.

steps.instruction: Wet the bed and let it bloom.
Pour in slow circles to 300 g.
Pour to the final weight.
Let it drain fully.

recipes.name: Light
recipes.tuningNote: Less coffee for the water makes a lighter pot for sipping all morning.

steps.instruction: Fill the reservoir and fill the basket.
Start the machine.
Swirl the pot before you pour.
